scene_summary: A small office with a blind-covered window, low wooden cubby shelf, floor lamp, two rolling chairs, tables, and a large potted plant.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction captures the main office furnishings and their broad arrangement, particularly the shelf beneath the window, the lamp to its left, and the pair of chairs. However, the elevated, pulled-back view substantially changes the composition, the prominent dark paneled door is not visibly reproduced, and the floor and tabletop materials differ conspicuously.

main_defects.description: The large dark, rectangular paneled door visible on the right-hand wall is not recognizable in the reconstruction; only a narrow dark edge is visible near the right wall.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a broad dark door with eight inset panels, whereas the reconstruction's right side shows no comparable door face or panels.
main_defects.uncertainty: The changed viewpoint and partial wall occlusion may hide some or all of the door, so its absence from the underlying scene cannot be established.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction is viewed from much farther back and higher, exposing the open tops and exterior of the walls and much more empty floor, rather than the close interior perspective of the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference fills the image with interior walls and nearby furniture; the reconstruction shows a dollhouse-like room against a gray background and smaller, more distant objects.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent differences in object size and placement follow from this viewpoint change.

main_defects.description: The floor is much paler and more uniformly tiled, and the tabletops are light gray rather than the darker gray surfaces in the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a medium-brown, visibly variegated wood-like floor and dark gray tabletops; the reconstruction has nearly white floor boards and pale tabletops.
main_defects.uncertainty: Different lighting and exposure may contribute to the color contrast.

main_defects.description: The chairs appear more separated and aligned along the room depth, with the rear chair directly in front of the shelving, whereas the reference chairs are arranged more side by side across the center of the room.
main_defects.evidence: In the reference the chair seats occupy left-center and right-center positions; in the reconstruction one is visually behind the other near the shelf and the second is farther forward.
main_defects.uncertainty: The different camera angle may explain part of the apparent separation and alignment.

main_defects.description: The blind and surrounding frame occupy a noticeably smaller portion of the back wall relative to the shelf than in the reference.
main_defects.evidence: The reference window is approximately as wide as the shelf and visually dominates the wall; the reconstruction window is smaller and less prominent above the shelf.
main_defects.uncertainty: Perspective and framing affect apparent proportions, and the rear chair partially obscures the reconstruction shelf.

strengths: The blind-covered window sits above a light wood cubby shelf, with a slender floor lamp on the left and a narrow white cabinet on the right.
Two light-colored molded rolling chairs, rectangular tables, and a spiky plant in a teal pot reproduce the main furniture types.
The pale walls, wood-toned shelving, and horizontal blinds preserve the reference's broad color arrangement.
uncertainty: This is a coarse automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. The images use substantially different viewpoints, and occlusion or cropping can make objects appear missing or misplaced without establishing the underlying geometry.
